text:
sam: Quick heads-up — profiler shows a regression after the multi-variant routing change.

sam: Baseline continuous-batching latency P95 went from 85ms -> 132ms for short-seq (<=64) in the canary.

nina: ack. Which part of the stack? kernel selection, batching, or KV cache?

sam: Initial diff points to batching formation; when compat-sets are enabled we get more fragmented batches. Kernel selector also flips more often due to mixed sequence lengths, so kernel-switching overhead increases.

devin: Interesting. I saw the same in a microbench — payloads that could be grouped before are now queued separately because routing enforces variant compatibility.

maria: Do we have numbers on batch sizes / queue wait times pre/post?

sam: Yes. Short summary from profiling run (canary):
```
pre-change: avg batch size = 12 reqs, avg queue wait = 6.8ms, token throughput = 92k toks/s
post-change: avg batch size = 7 reqs, avg queue wait = 14.2ms, token throughput = 66k toks/s
kernel-switch overhead: ~3.4ms additional per batch when mixed kernel path toggles
```

aditya: Also saw KV cache miss amplification — fallbacks to compatibility variants cause cache keys to diverge, lower hit rate by ~9%. That increases decode token work.

nina: So two failure modes: (1) smaller/more frequent batches, (2) worse KV cache utilization. Both hurt P95.

devin: For batching heuristics we can try: prefer cross-variant batching when models are ABI-compatible and kernel path identical. Add a soft token-budget target to avoid tiny batches for short sequences.

maria: Can we get a quick classifier that says "safe-to-co-batch" for variant pairs? It would be a compat-set augmentation rather than strict separation.

sam: I prototyped a compat-scoring heuristic: pair score = kernel_compat * (1 - seq_length_std/mean) * kv_key_overlap. If score > 0.78 allow co-batching. Preliminary run increased avg batch size to 10 and recovered ~65% of lost throughput.

aditya: Nice. For KV cache we might canonicalize cache keys across minor variant differences when the weight layout is same and tokenizer identical. That requires onboarding metadata from model catalog.

nina: Also need queue policy changes: current FIFO with max_batch_timeout=10ms. Suggest implementing token-budget-aware batching: hold until either max_time OR tokens_in_batch >= token_budget. token_budget should be adaptive per route/model-group.

devin: Agreed. For short-seq optimized routes, token_budget=256 (tokens) seems fine; for long-runner routes token_budget can be 1024. We should simulate with real traffic traces.

sam: Action items:
- sam: roll out compat-scoring prototype to canary and capture metrics (avg batch size, KV hit rate, P50/P95) — WIP
- nina: add token-budget knob to runtime config and a simple adaptive policy (start budget=256, adjust +/-20% on throughput feedback) — PR?
- aditya: add cache-key canonicalization proof-of-concept for tokenizer-identical variants — will test on staging catalog
- devin: run replay tests with mixed-model trace and report perf deltas (use 3 hour sampled trace)

maria: Also: let's add telemetry for kernel-switch events per-batch so we can correlate with latency spikes.

infra-bot: deploy request queued for canary (redwood-runtime-canary). ID: deploy-20260312-89fa

sam: Thanks. If we can get the compat-scoring + token-budget tweak in canary this week we should see P95 move back toward baseline. Will post numbers once infra-bot finishes deploy. :thumbsup:

nina: If anyone hits perf cliffs, tag me and @sam. I'll prioritize.

aditya: FYI I observed a regression scenario: when fallback occurs to CPU-optimized variant, kernel switch + cold KV causes ~220ms tail. Need fallback policy to prefer GPU-compatible fallbacks when latency budget tight.

sam: Good call. Add to backlog: fallback preference ordering by latency SLO, not only compatibility.

devin: I'll add tests to the regression harness to ensure we don't reintroduce the same perf drop.

sam: Closing loop — will update thread with canary numbers once available.
